claim.value: The comparison should use the same predefined interval after placement for inspection because delayed uploads and persistent backlogs can obscure the response.
claim.scope: Timing of attachment inspection in the prospective comparison; consistent intervals are prescribed without a claim that they eliminate all distortion.

provenance.rationale: P009 prescribes the common predefined inspection interval; P026 supplies its rationale and identifies delayed uploads and backlogs as possible distortions.

signal_basis.value: Compare missing-attachment frequency before and after responsibility becomes explicit using comparable covered orders and a common predefined inspection interval. The proposed signal is a reduction repeated across comparable observation periods if volume permits. Delayed uploads and backlogs may obscure that response, so distinguish new orders from backlog repairs.
signal_basis.scope: Prospective attachment-frequency comparison, with inspection timing standardized and backlog repairs distinguished from new orders.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply the comparison, observed signal, volume qualification, inspection timing and backlog distinction.
The bounded methodological claim is supported without an unresolved empirical bridge.

rationale: Attachment status can depend on elapsed time after placement when uploads are delayed. A common inspection interval therefore supports comparability of the measured response. Backlogs provide an additional reason for caution and separate treatment. This licenses the prescribed timing control within the claim's explicit limit that it need not eliminate all distortion.
uncertainty: The amount of remaining distortion is unspecified, but the claim does not assert its elimination or quantify the benefit of standardized timing.
